problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{2x{y}^{2}-1}{{x}^{2}y}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{2h(x,y)}{{x}^{3}y}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y)=\frac{x+y}{\operatorname{sin}⁡y},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(\pi ,\frac{\pi }{2}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x+y}{\operatorname{sin}⁡y}) & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+y)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡y-(x+y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y)}{{sin}^{2}⁡y} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡y-(x+y)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y}{{sin}^{2}⁡y} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡y-(x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{{sin}^{2}⁡y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(\pi ,\frac{\pi }{2}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(\pi ,\pi /2)} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-(\pi +\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{1-0}{{1}^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
